name: Cable Pull-Through
summary: A cable hip-hinge exercise that teaches and trains hip extension for the glutes and hamstrings, with constant tension and low spinal load.
setup: Attach a rope to a low pulley.
Stand facing away from the machine, straddle the cable and hold the rope between your legs with both hands.
Walk forward until the cable has tension and set your feet about shoulder width apart.
Keep a soft knee bend and a flat back.
execution: Push your hips straight back, letting the rope pass between your legs.
Keep your back flat and arms straight as you hinge until you feel a hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward by squeezing your glutes.
Stand tall at the top without leaning back.
cues: Squeeze the glutes at the top
mistakes: Squatting instead of hinging: send the hips back with a fixed knee angle.
Pulling with the arms: keep arms straight and move at the hips.
Leaning back at the top: finish standing tall.
Rounding the back: reduce the weight and brace your trunk.
